videos.title: A crate of apples is not a crate of fruit: one list with two labels lets a lemon in, so a list you can write to must match its type exactly
An apple dispenser only hands apples out, so with out a Dispenser<Apple> passes as a Dispenser<Fruit>
The compost bin takes any fruit, so a Bin<Fruit> stands in for a Bin<Apple>: in flips the arrow
Erasure tears the label off; inline with reified copies it onto a note at every call
A pattern switch is a clerk with a printed sheet: checked for every kind of item and read from the top, while an instanceof chain is checked by nobody
A decorator wraps the same interface and passes the call on; move the cap inside the heavy parcel rule and 8.00 becomes 11.00
A fuse box for the van company: the circuit breaker counts failures, trips, turns callers away at once, and lets one probe test the line
Inline as a photocopy, not a slip: the compiler pastes a small helper and its lambda into each caller
The cloakroom ticket: a delegated property is a hidden delegate field plus a getter and setter that call getValue and setValue
Three handlers each read a scan's raw fields and fail in their own ways; a sealed model, value classes and one parse at the door check each scan once
Units at the parcel desk: a value class is its own type to the compiler and a plain long at run time
A box whose label wore off: List<*> reads as Any?, takes nothing in, and is not the drawer MutableList<Any?>
Keep the routine and pass in the one decision: a comparator ranks the couriers, and a stable sort keeps a tie in its order
A box of Any lets the wrong thing in and fails at the counter; Box<T> puts a blank on the label that each caller fills, and the compiler checks every put
A name your block lacks falls through to the outer builder; @DslMarker on every builder makes each section of the order form offer only its own boxes
A box asks what it holds: one recursive price function prices a box of boxes, and a copied list keeps the box taped shut
Answer it, or pass it on: a complaint travels along the shop's desk, each handler answers or calls next, and the order of the list is behavior
Everyone on the sign-up sheet hears the news, each in its own try with a way out; a command slip goes on the history only after it worked
A List runs each step over the whole tray; a Sequence sends one cookie down the whole line and stops early, but sortedBy still reads every recipe
Two questions pick a scope function: is the value this or it, and does the call hand back the value or the block's result
Fail fast with either { } when each step needs the one before; collect every error with zipOrAccumulate when the checks are independent
A pure core decides from plain values, the clock included, and a thin shell reads, calls the core and does the errands
A pure function is like a recipe card: same ingredients, same result, kitchen left as it was; a hidden clock or global breaks it
A closure is a recipe card with a note pinned on, and a captured var is one shared box, so two threads lose updates on it
Pass in the work, not its answer: retry takes the call as a function, so one loop serves every flaky call
fold carries one reading past every cookie, like a jar on the kitchen scale; reduce has no start and throws on an empty day
For this job, take-only: Array<out Fruit> lets one function read a busy crate, while Java arrays only find out at run time
An inspector with a different check for each kind of goods: Visitor puts each job in one class, and a sealed switch does the same job with less
A plain T can only do what Any? does; an upper bound such as T : Fruit is a fruit-only sign that shuts some callers out and lets the body weigh and compare
A sealed type prints every box on the form: javac and the JVM refuse an unlisted subtype, and a switch without default finds the new one
A base-class setter forgets the subclass; with B : Builder<B> each kind of form writes its own name in the blank, so grams returns a GiftBoxBuilder and the chain keeps ribbon
Like asking the baker for a loaf, the shop asks for a messenger and never names the class: a function hands it in, and a switch with no default lets the compiler find the new case
Like a travel plug, an adapter fits the courier's old client to the shop's own port and translates calls, answers and errors, so their IOException stops at the edge
A copy copies the arrow, not the list: two carts share one list until the list can't change, and copy() even skips a private constructor unless init does the checking
An object knows only its class: KClass and Class are one note on two kinds of paper, and only a KType, written by the compiler at a call site, keeps the whole label
Eight threads ask for the one price list and get eight; an enum, the holder idiom or double-checked locking makes the others wait, and the best singleton is passed in
Typed keys: the key carries its value's type, so a read needs no cast and same-named keys don't collide, and the key stays invariant because it writes too
A record is a form in a clear sleeve: javac writes every method from one list, the compact constructor checks every copy, and the promise stops at the attached list
The compiler smart-casts only from checks it can see; a contract is the stamp on the outside of the envelope, believed and never checked
An annotation is only a note on the ticket; compiler plugins are the machines that act on it: all-open drops final, no-arg adds a blank constructor, serialization writes a serializer
One reply form allows 48 shapes and 3 make sense: three records under a sealed interface, one clerk at the door, and the rules in functions
A board keyed by exact class never rings ParcelEvent's bell; one publish walks the event's supertypes, nearest first, and caches those keys per class

Java sees only the class file: default arguments, a reified subscribe, object members and value classes each look odd or go missing there, and Class overloads, @JvmOverloads, @JvmStatic and a facade that still validates fix them
